# Introduction

## Purpose

This notebook is **Step 4** of the PICRUSt2 workflow. It performs community-level (per-sample) functional differential abundance analysis (DAA) on the unstratified PICRUSt2 output from [Step 2](2_picrust2_pipeline.md) — asking which predicted pathways differ between study conditions and whether two complementary methods agree — using the [ggpicrust2](https://github.com/cafferychen777/ggpicrust2) R package.

Every feature analyzed here is at **pathway level**, not gene level: MetaCyc pathways (computed natively by PICRUSt2) and KEGG pathways (derived from PICRUSt2's KO gene-family predictions by aggregation — see [Why Two Functional Levels?] below). Raw KO and EC gene-family abundances are not tested directly in this notebook.

::: {.alert .alert-info}
**Want to identify which taxa drive selected pathways?** [Step 5 — Taxon Contribution Analysis](5_taxon_contribution.md) traces selected MetaCyc and KEGG pathway predictions back to their contributing ASVs and taxonomy labels.
:::

## Why Two Functional Levels?

-   **[MetaCyc](https://metacyc.org/) pathways** — PICRUSt2 computes these natively ([pathways_out/path_abun_unstrat.tsv](../../results/2_picrust2_pipeline/picrust2_out_pipeline/pathways_out/path_abun_unstrat.tsv), via MinPath applied to its EC-number predictions). Annotation uses `ggpicrust2`'s bundled MetaCyc reference table; no internet access required.
-   **[KEGG](https://www.genome.jp/kegg/pathway.html) pathways** — PICRUSt2 does **not** compute a KEGG-pathway abundance table directly; it only predicts per-KO (gene-family) abundance. `ggpicrust2::ko2kegg_abundance()` aggregates that KO table with the PICRUSt2-style upper-half mean *before* statistical testing, so DAA is run on pathways, never on individual KOs. Its `filter_for_prokaryotes = TRUE` option removes broad Organismal Systems and most Human Diseases categories, but it does **not** guarantee that every host-, eukaryote-, or virus-associated pathway map is absent: individual KOs are shared across pathway maps and across the tree of life. KEGG results therefore include explicit interpretation flags for configured host-associated maps and must be reviewed using their pathway name and hierarchy before biological reporting. Names and hierarchy classes come from `ggpicrust2`'s bundled KEGG reference, making conversion and annotation reproducible without live API calls.

Neither level involves gene/enzyme-level (raw KO or EC) differential abundance testing.

## Why LinDA and MaAsLin2?

PICRUSt2 pathway abundances are **predicted functional profiles**, not directly observed pathway sequencing counts. Step 4 therefore excludes count-model methods that would require treating the mostly fractional predictions as observed integer counts, and it excludes LEfSe from significance testing. It retains two complementary sample-level approaches:

-   **LinDA** applies a centered log-ratio transformation and bias correction designed for high-dimensional compositional abundance data.
-   **MaAsLin2** applies total-sum scaling, an arcsine-square-root transformation, and a linear model. This provides a differently transformed regression analysis without adding another count-likelihood method.

The methods are reported separately. `Method_Agreement` indicates whether both adjusted p-values pass the configured threshold; it is a convergence check, not a majority vote and not a new p-value. A pathway detected by only one method remains method-dependent. Neither method propagates uncertainty from PICRUSt2's genome-content prediction, so every result must be described as an association with **predicted functional potential**, not a measured pathway difference.

Every DAA comparison is strictly two-condition: the reference `Condition` (marked `Reference = TRUE` in `data/metadata.tsv`) against exactly one other `Condition` at a time, repeated independently once per non-reference `Condition` level (see [Run the Selected DAA Methods]). The reference condition is the only condition any other condition is compared against.

## Statistics and Calculations

- **Prevalence filter:** by default, a pathway is tested only when its predicted
  abundance is non-zero in at least `min_nonzero_samples` across the full
  functional-level table. This pooled filter does not use condition labels and
  retains possible presence/absence differences. Every workbook also reports
  per-condition non-zero sample counts, prevalence percentages, structural-zero
  flags, and below-threshold boundary-case flags. When
  `strict_pairwise_prevalence_filter = TRUE`, each reference-versus-comparison
  model additionally requires at least `min_nonzero_samples` non-zero values in
  **each** of its two conditions; this stricter option is deliberately off by
  default because it removes complete presence/absence contrasts.
- **LinDA:** applies a centered log-ratio representation and estimates a
  bias-corrected linear-model association appropriate for compositional
  abundance profiles.
- **MaAsLin2:** in this `ggpicrust2::pathway_daa()` workflow, applies
  total-sum scaling, arcsine-square-root transformation, and a linear model.
  It is retained as a complementary transformed regression approach rather
  than a second count-likelihood model.
- **Multiple testing:** raw p-values are adjusted with the configured
  `p_adjust_method` (Benjamini-Hochberg by default) independently within each
  method, functional level, and reference-versus-comparison call. Statistical
  significance is based on the adjusted-p threshold, not the raw p-value. This
  controls FDR within each such family; it does not provide one study-wide FDR
  guarantee across both functional levels or across multiple comparisons.
- **Descriptive effect summaries:** condition means and sample standard
  deviations are calculated from retained predicted abundances. Relative
  abundance divides each condition mean by the sum of retained pathway means
  for that condition. The reported log2 fold-change is
  `log2((comparison mean + pseudocount)/(reference mean + pseudocount))`, where
  the pseudocount is half the smallest positive condition mean in that
  functional level.
- **Method agreement:** the two adjusted p-values remain separate.
  `Method_Agreement` only describes whether zero, one, or both methods cross
  the threshold; it is not a meta-analysis, combined p-value, or extra test.
- **Sample size and power:** the condition sample counts are derived from
  `data/metadata.tsv` and printed during the run. Small groups reduce power,
  make sparse/boundary estimates less stable, and can produce fragile adjusted
  p-values when hundreds of pathways are tested. Results from small cohorts
  should be treated as hypothesis-generating until independently validated.
- **KEGG interpretation:** `filter_for_prokaryotes = TRUE` reduces broad
  eukaryotic/human categories but cannot establish that every retained map is a
  biologically coherent bacterial pathway. Configured host-associated pathway
  IDs are flagged, not silently deleted, so the underlying KO signal remains
  auditable without inviting pathway-name over-interpretation.
## Prerequisites

Before running this notebook, ensure that:

1.  Required R packages are installed — run [setup/install_R_dependencies.R](../../setup/install_R_dependencies.R) once per R environment (this installs `ggpicrust2`, LinDA's `MicrobiomeStat` backend, and MaAsLin2 alongside the packages needed for the other workflow steps).
2.  **[Step 2](2_picrust2_pipeline.md)** has been completed successfully, producing [pred_metagenome_unstrat.tsv](../../results/2_picrust2_pipeline/picrust2_out_pipeline/KO_metagenome_out/pred_metagenome_unstrat.tsv) and [path_abun_unstrat.tsv](../../results/2_picrust2_pipeline/picrust2_out_pipeline/pathways_out/path_abun_unstrat.tsv) in [results/2_picrust2_pipeline/picrust2_out_pipeline/](../../results/2_picrust2_pipeline/picrust2_out_pipeline/).
3.  **[data/metadata.tsv](../../data/metadata.tsv)** has been filled in with real sample metadata (see [data/README.md](../../data/README.md)) — every sample in the PICRUSt2 output must have a matching row with a `Condition` value, and exactly one complete `Condition` must be marked `Reference = TRUE` (the reference/control condition every other condition is compared against; see [Load Metadata]).

## What This Notebook Does

1.  **Imports** the unstratified KO and MetaCyc pathway abundance tables produced by Step 2 and validates that every sample matches a row in [data/metadata.tsv](../../data/metadata.tsv).
2.  **Prepares both functional levels**: the MetaCyc pathway table is used as-is; the KO table is converted to KEGG pathway abundance via `ggpicrust2::ko2kegg_abundance()`.
3.  For **each** functional level, applies the pooled prevalence filter, computes condition-specific prevalence diagnostics, optionally applies the stricter prevalence requirement within each pairwise comparison, and removes any sample with zero variance across the retained features (a degenerate input that silently crashes several DAA backends if left in).
4.  **Runs LinDA and MaAsLin2** for each level, as a series of strictly two-condition comparisons — the reference condition (derived from [data/metadata.tsv](../../data/metadata.tsv)'s `Reference` column; see [Load Metadata]) against exactly one other `Condition` at a time, repeated for every non-reference `Condition`. Any single (method, comparison) failure is caught, reported in the rendered notebook, and does not stop the other method or comparison from running.
5.  **Annotates** every feature retained after prevalence filtering (once per feature, regardless of how many methods tested it) from `ggpicrust2`'s bundled MetaCyc or KEGG reference tables; KEGG annotations include an explicit interpretation flag and note for configured host-associated maps.
6.  **Computes condition-wise summary statistics** (mean, SD, relative abundance, non-zero sample count, prevalence percentage, structural-zero/boundary flags, and log2 fold-change vs. the reference condition) driven entirely by [data/metadata.tsv](../../data/metadata.tsv)'s `Condition` column — no hardcoded sample-column positions.
7.  **Builds one combined `Abundance_Summary` sheet**, one results sheet per DAA method, and a per-pathway `Method_Agreement` sheet containing both methods' adjusted p-values, significance codes, agreement status, and pairwise prevalence diagnostics.
8.  **Exports** every table to two separate Excel workbooks, one per functional level, each with its own trailing `Column_Dictionary` sheet.

## Expected Input

-   [results/2_picrust2_pipeline/picrust2_out_pipeline/KO_metagenome_out/pred_metagenome_unstrat.tsv](../../results/2_picrust2_pipeline/picrust2_out_pipeline/KO_metagenome_out/pred_metagenome_unstrat.tsv) — per-sample KO abundance (converted to KEGG pathway abundance here).
-   [results/2_picrust2_pipeline/picrust2_out_pipeline/pathways_out/path_abun_unstrat.tsv](../../results/2_picrust2_pipeline/picrust2_out_pipeline/pathways_out/path_abun_unstrat.tsv) — per-sample MetaCyc pathway abundance.
-   [data/metadata.tsv](../../data/metadata.tsv) — sample metadata with the required `SampleID`, `Condition`, and `Reference` columns.

## Expected Output

-   [results/4_functional_differential_abundance_analysis/functional_daa_summary_MetaCyc.xlsx](../../results/4_functional_differential_abundance_analysis/functional_daa_summary_MetaCyc.xlsx) — MetaCyc-level results: `Abundance_Summary`, `LinDA`, `Maaslin2`, `Method_Agreement`, and `Column_Dictionary`.
-   [results/4_functional_differential_abundance_analysis/functional_daa_summary_KEGG.xlsx](../../results/4_functional_differential_abundance_analysis/functional_daa_summary_KEGG.xlsx) — the same set of sheets for the KEGG level.

# Environment Setup

## Load Required Packages {#load-packages}

The chunk below loads every R package this notebook depends on -- principally [ggpicrust2](https://github.com/cafferychen777/ggpicrust2) for corrected KO-to-KEGG-pathway conversion, bundled pathway references, and the LinDA/MaAsLin2 `pathway_daa()` interface -- plus the helper functions shared across the workflow, each sourced from [R/functions/](../functions/).

```{r load-packages, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# NOTE: This chunk assumes the packages below are already installed. If any
# library() call fails with "there is no package called ...", run
# setup/install_R_dependencies.R once to install every package this
# workflow needs, then re-run this notebook.

library(here)         # Project-relative file paths
library(readr)        # Fast, consistent delimited-file import
library(dplyr)         # Data manipulation grammar (filter/mutate/summarise/join)
library(tidyr)         # Reshaping between wide and long formats
library(tibble)        # Modern data frames with explicit rownames-as-column handling
library(ggpicrust2)    # PICRUSt2 output analysis: ko2kegg_abundance(), pathway_daa(),
                        # pathway_annotation().
library(openxlsx)      # Excel file creation and manipulation

# Version 2.5.16 fixes the broad KEGG Organismal Systems/Human Diseases filter
# and the upper-half pathway-abundance calculation used below. Even current
# releases can retain individual host/eukaryote/virus-associated maps outside
# those broad categories; those are flagged explicitly during annotation.
minimum_ggpicrust2_version <- package_version("2.5.16")
if (packageVersion("ggpicrust2") < minimum_ggpicrust2_version) {
  stop(
    "Step 4 requires ggpicrust2 >= ", minimum_ggpicrust2_version,
    " for corrected KEGG aggregation and prokaryote filtering. Installed: ",
    packageVersion("ggpicrust2"), ". Re-run setup/install_R_dependencies.R."
  )
}

# Source the custom Excel utility functions from the project's function library
source(here("R", "functions", "add_sheet_to_excel_function.R"))
source(here("R", "functions", "build_column_dictionary_function.R"))
source(here("R", "functions", "render_output_links_function.R"))
# Source the custom render_output_tree utility function from the project's
# function library. This function prints this notebook's entire output
# folder as a clickable directory tree (used in "Output File Summary" below),
# scanned live from disk at knit time so it always matches what was actually
# produced on this run.
source(here("R", "functions", "render_output_tree_function.R"))
```

# Configuration

## Adjust Analysis Parameters {#adjust-analysis-parameters}

These are the settings you are most likely to want to change before running this notebook.

```{r define-analysis-parameters}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Functional levels to analyze. Both run by default (see "Why Two Functional
# Levels?" above). Conversion and annotation use bundled local references, so
# routine execution does not depend on a live KEGG API. Valid entries are
# "MetaCyc" and "KEGG".
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
functional_levels_to_analyze <- c("MetaCyc", "KEGG")  # <-- EDIT to c("MetaCyc") or c("KEGG") to run only one

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Selected differential-abundance methods passed to
# ggpicrust2::pathway_daa(), once per method and pairwise comparison.
# This set is intentionally restricted to two complementary sample-level
# approaches suitable for predicted compositional pathway profiles. Do not
# add count-model or LEfSe methods to the significance agreement summary.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
daa_methods_to_run <- c("LinDA", "Maaslin2")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Comparison variable required by the workflow's documented metadata schema.
# The reference/baseline level every
# other condition is compared against is intentionally NOT set here: it is
# derived automatically, in the Load Metadata step below, from
# data/metadata.tsv's Reference column (TRUE for the reference condition's rows,
# FALSE for every other row — see data/README.md). Declaring the reference
# condition inside the metadata file itself, rather than as a notebook
# parameter, means it can never silently drift out of sync with the data.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
group_column <- "Condition"

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Multiple-testing correction method passed to p_adjust_method, and the
# adjusted-p-value cutoff used for per-method significance and method
# agreement. Asterisk codes retain their conventional fixed 0.05/0.01/0.001/
# 0.0001 boundaries so their meaning does not change when the agreement
# threshold is customized.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
p_adjust_method       <- "BH"    # <-- EDIT: any method accepted by stats::p.adjust()
significance_threshold <- 0.05   # <-- EDIT: adjusted-p-value cutoff for "significant"

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Minimum number of samples in which a feature must have a non-zero
# abundance value to be retained by the pooled, condition-blind filter.
# Applied independently per functional level, since MetaCyc and KEGG
# prevalence can differ for the same sample set.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
min_nonzero_samples <- 3  # <-- EDIT to make prevalence filtering stricter/looser

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Optional stricter filter applied independently inside each reference-versus-
# comparison call. FALSE preserves possible presence/absence differences and
# reports them with explicit prevalence/boundary flags. TRUE requires at least
# min_nonzero_samples non-zero values in BOTH conditions before a feature is
# passed to either DAA method for that comparison.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
strict_pairwise_prevalence_filter <- FALSE  # <-- EDIT to TRUE for strict within-pair filtering

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# KEGG maps that warrant explicit host/eukaryote/virus interpretation review
# even after ggpicrust2's broad prokaryote filter. These maps are FLAGGED, not
# deleted: shared KOs can be genuine microbial genes even when the pathway-map
# label describes a host or viral process. Keep this documented vector current
# if a different ggpicrust2/KEGG reference release is adopted.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
kegg_host_associated_pathway_ids <- c(
  "ko04330", # Notch signaling pathway
  "ko04024", # cAMP signaling pathway
  "ko04145", # Phagosome
  "ko04148", # Efferocytosis
  "ko03250"  # Viral life cycle - HIV-1
)

# Validate every configurable analysis setting before importing large tables.
valid_functional_levels <- c("MetaCyc", "KEGG")
invalid_functional_levels <- setdiff(
  functional_levels_to_analyze, valid_functional_levels
)
if (length(functional_levels_to_analyze) == 0L ||
    length(invalid_functional_levels) > 0L ||
    anyDuplicated(functional_levels_to_analyze)) {
  stop(
    "functional_levels_to_analyze must contain unique entries from: ",
    paste(valid_functional_levels, collapse = ", ")
  )
}
required_daa_methods <- c("LinDA", "Maaslin2")
if (!setequal(daa_methods_to_run, required_daa_methods) ||
    length(daa_methods_to_run) != length(required_daa_methods)) {
  stop(
    "daa_methods_to_run is intentionally restricted to the two reliable, ",
    "non-redundant methods: LinDA and Maaslin2."
  )
}
if (!(p_adjust_method %in% stats::p.adjust.methods)) {
  stop("p_adjust_method must be accepted by stats::p.adjust(); received: ",
       p_adjust_method)
}
if (length(significance_threshold) != 1L || is.na(significance_threshold) ||
    !is.finite(significance_threshold) || significance_threshold <= 0 ||
    significance_threshold >= 1) {
  stop("significance_threshold must be one finite number strictly between 0 and 1.")
}
if (length(min_nonzero_samples) != 1L || is.na(min_nonzero_samples) ||
    !is.finite(min_nonzero_samples) || min_nonzero_samples < 1 ||
    min_nonzero_samples != floor(min_nonzero_samples)) {
  stop("min_nonzero_samples must be one positive whole number.")
}
if (!is.logical(strict_pairwise_prevalence_filter) ||
    length(strict_pairwise_prevalence_filter) != 1L ||
    is.na(strict_pairwise_prevalence_filter)) {
  stop("strict_pairwise_prevalence_filter must be exactly TRUE or FALSE.")
}
if (anyDuplicated(kegg_host_associated_pathway_ids) ||
    any(!grepl("^ko[0-9]{5}$", kegg_host_associated_pathway_ids))) {
  stop(
    "kegg_host_associated_pathway_ids must contain unique KEGG pathway IDs ",
    "in ko##### format."
  )
}

cat(
  "Step 4 Configuration:\n",
  "- Functional levels:", paste(functional_levels_to_analyze, collapse = ", "), "\n",
  "- DAA methods:", paste(daa_methods_to_run, collapse = ", "), "\n",
  "- Comparison column:", group_column, "\n",
  "- Reference condition: (derived from data/metadata.tsv's Reference column in the Load Metadata step below)\n",
  "- p-value adjustment:", p_adjust_method, "\n",
  "- Significance threshold (adjusted p):", significance_threshold, "\n",
  "- Minimum non-zero samples per feature:", min_nonzero_samples, "\n",
  "- Strict pairwise prevalence filter:", strict_pairwise_prevalence_filter, "\n",
  "- KEGG pathway IDs flagged for host/eukaryote/virus interpretation review:",
  paste(kegg_host_associated_pathway_ids, collapse = ", "), "\n"
)
```

## Define Path Parameters {#define-paths}

This chunk resolves every input and output path relative to the project root via `here()`, creates this step's own output folder if it does not already exist, and fails fast with an informative error if Step 2's output or [data/metadata.tsv](../../data/metadata.tsv) cannot be found -- distinguishing a genuinely missing [Step 2](2_picrust2_pipeline.md) run from output that is still gzip-compressed, so the error message points at the real fix.

```{r define-paths}
# Base folders
results_folder <- here("results")
data_folder    <- here("data")

# Step 2's output (this notebook's input)
step2_output_folder <- here(results_folder, "2_picrust2_pipeline")
step2_run_dir        <- here(step2_output_folder, "picrust2_out_pipeline")

input_ko_path       <- here(step2_run_dir, "KO_metagenome_out", "pred_metagenome_unstrat.tsv")
input_pathway_path  <- here(step2_run_dir, "pathways_out", "path_abun_unstrat.tsv")
input_metadata_path <- here(data_folder, "metadata.tsv")

# This notebook's own output folder.
output_folder <- here(results_folder, "4_functional_differential_abundance_analysis")
dir.create(output_folder, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# One Excel workbook PER functional level, rather than a single combined
# workbook, so MetaCyc and KEGG results can be opened, filtered, and shared
# independently of one another.
output_excel_path_by_level <- list(
  MetaCyc = here(output_folder, "functional_daa_summary_MetaCyc.xlsx"),
  KEGG = here(output_folder, "functional_daa_summary_KEGG.xlsx")
)

# Confirm the expected inputs actually exist before going any further.
# picrust2_pipeline.py leaves both files gzip-compressed unless
# decompress_output_files was TRUE in Step 2 — check for the .gz variant
# too so the error message points at the real fix (decompress, don't re-run
# Step 2) rather than implying the run itself is missing.
check_input_exists <- function(path, step_label) {
  if (file.exists(path)) return(invisible(TRUE))
  gz_path <- paste0(path, ".gz")
  if (file.exists(gz_path)) {
    stop(
      "Found a compressed but not decompressed input: ", gz_path, "\n",
      "Re-run Step 2 with decompress_output_files <- TRUE, or manually ",
      "decompress this file, then re-run this notebook."
    )
  }
  stop(
    "Could not find the expected input file: ", path, "\n",
    "Run Step 2 (2_picrust2_pipeline.Rmd) first."
  )
}
check_input_exists(input_ko_path, "Step 2")
check_input_exists(input_pathway_path, "Step 2")
if (!file.exists(input_metadata_path)) {
  stop(
    "Could not find the metadata file: ", input_metadata_path, "\n",
    "See data/README.md for the required format."
  )
}

cat(
  "Path Configuration:\n",
  "- KO abundance input:", input_ko_path, "\n",
  "- MetaCyc pathway abundance input:", input_pathway_path, "\n",
  "- Metadata input:", input_metadata_path, "\n",
  "- Output folder:", output_folder, "\n"
)
```

# Import and Validate Input Data

## Load Metadata {#load-metadata}

This chunk reads [data/metadata.tsv](../../data/metadata.tsv) and validates it thoroughly before anything downstream uses it: confirms the required `SampleID`, `Condition`, and `Reference` columns are present, coerces `Reference` to logical, checks that every `Condition` is internally consistent (wholly reference or wholly not), and confirms exactly one `Condition` is marked as the reference -- since every DAA comparison in this notebook is built around that single reference `Condition` (see [Why LinDA and MaAsLin2?] above).

```{r load-metadata}
sample_metadata <- read_tsv(input_metadata_path, show_col_types = FALSE, trim_ws = TRUE)

required_metadata_columns <- c("SampleID", group_column, "Reference")
missing_metadata_columns <- setdiff(
  required_metadata_columns, colnames(sample_metadata)
)
if (length(missing_metadata_columns) > 0L) {
  stop(
    "data/metadata.tsv is missing required column(s): ",
    paste(missing_metadata_columns, collapse = ", "),
    ". Expected: ", paste(required_metadata_columns, collapse = ", ")
  )
}
unexpected_metadata_columns <- setdiff(
  colnames(sample_metadata), required_metadata_columns
)
if (length(unexpected_metadata_columns) > 0L) {
  stop(
    "data/metadata.tsv must use the simplified three-column schema exactly. ",
    "Unexpected column(s): ", paste(unexpected_metadata_columns, collapse = ", "),
    ". Expected: ", paste(required_metadata_columns, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

if (anyDuplicated(sample_metadata$SampleID)) {
  stop("data/metadata.tsv contains duplicate SampleID values; each sample must occur exactly once.")
}
if (any(is.na(sample_metadata$SampleID) | trimws(sample_metadata$SampleID) == "")) {
  stop("data/metadata.tsv contains an empty SampleID value.")
}
if (any(is.na(sample_metadata[[group_column]]) | trimws(sample_metadata[[group_column]]) == "")) {
  stop("data/metadata.tsv contains an empty ", group_column, " value.")
}
# read_tsv() already parses an unquoted TRUE/FALSE column as logical; coerce
# defensively in case the source file wrote it as a quoted string, "True"/
# "False", or 1/0 instead.
reference_group_flag <- if (is.logical(sample_metadata$Reference)) {
  sample_metadata$Reference
} else {
  as.logical(sample_metadata$Reference)
}
if (any(is.na(reference_group_flag))) {
  stop(
    "data/metadata.tsv's 'Reference' column contains value(s) that could not ",
    "be interpreted as TRUE/FALSE. Use exactly TRUE or FALSE for every row -- ",
    "see data/README.md."
  )
}
sample_metadata$Reference <- reference_group_flag

# Every row of a given Condition must agree on Reference -- a Condition is
# either wholly the reference or wholly not. Catch a partially-marked Condition
# here with a clear error rather than silently deriving an inconsistent
# reference_group downstream.
reference_flag_by_group <- sample_metadata %>%
  group_by(.data[[group_column]]) %>%
  summarise(n_distinct_flags = n_distinct(Reference), .groups = "drop")
inconsistent_groups <- reference_flag_by_group[[group_column]][reference_flag_by_group$n_distinct_flags > 1]
if (length(inconsistent_groups) > 0) {
  stop(
    "data/metadata.tsv's 'Reference' column is not consistent within ", group_column,
    " group(s): ", paste(inconsistent_groups, collapse = ", "),
    ". Every row of a given ", group_column, " must share the same Reference value -- ",
    "see data/README.md."
  )
}

# Exactly one Condition must be marked as the reference condition.
groups_marked_as_reference <- unique(sample_metadata[[group_column]][sample_metadata$Reference])
if (length(groups_marked_as_reference) == 0) {
  stop(
    "No ", group_column, " is marked Reference = TRUE in data/metadata.tsv. ",
    "Exactly one ", group_column, " must be the reference condition -- see data/README.md."
  )
}
if (length(groups_marked_as_reference) > 1) {
  stop(
    "More than one ", group_column, " is marked Reference = TRUE in data/metadata.tsv: ",
    paste(groups_marked_as_reference, collapse = ", "),
    ". Exactly one ", group_column, " must be the reference condition -- see data/README.md."
  )
}

# The single Condition marked Reference = TRUE becomes the reference/
# control level every other Condition is compared against throughout this
# notebook -- and, per the pairwise DAA design below (see [Run All
# Requested DAA Methods]), the only condition every other condition is ever
# compared to (no comparison skips the reference condition).
reference_group <- groups_marked_as_reference

# ggpicrust2's pathway_daa() (which receives the full metadata data frame,
# rather than a single extracted vector) needs a sample-identifier column
# to match metadata rows against abundance-table columns. The CRAN release
# of ggpicrust2 (installed by setup/install_R_dependencies.R) still
# hard-requires that column to be named exactly `sample_name`; it does not
# yet accept `SampleID` even though `SampleID` is this workflow's own
# metadata standard (see data/README.md). Add a `sample_name` mirror of
# `SampleID` here, once, so every downstream call (both functional levels)
# has it available without duplicating this fix at each call site.
sample_metadata$sample_name <- sample_metadata$SampleID

group_sample_counts <- table(sample_metadata[[group_column]])
if (strict_pairwise_prevalence_filter &&
    any(group_sample_counts < min_nonzero_samples)) {
  undersized_groups <- names(group_sample_counts)[
    group_sample_counts < min_nonzero_samples
  ]
  stop(
    "strict_pairwise_prevalence_filter = TRUE requires at least ",
    min_nonzero_samples, " samples in every condition. Undersized condition(s): ",
    paste0(undersized_groups, " (n=", group_sample_counts[undersized_groups], ")",
           collapse = ", "), "."
  )
}

cat(
  "Metadata loaded:", nrow(sample_metadata), "samples,",
  length(unique(sample_metadata[[group_column]])), "unique", group_column, "levels:\n",
  paste(" -", table(sample_metadata[[group_column]])[unique(sample_metadata[[group_column]])],
        unique(sample_metadata[[group_column]]), collapse = "\n"), "\n",
  "- Reference/baseline condition (from the Reference column):", reference_group, "\n",
  "- Statistical-power note: condition sample sizes are ",
  paste0(names(group_sample_counts), " n=", as.integer(group_sample_counts),
         collapse = "; "),
  ". Small groups reduce power and make sparse/boundary estimates less stable; ",
  "treat discoveries as hypothesis-generating when replication is limited.\n",
  sep = ""
)
```

## Load KO and MetaCyc Pathway Abundance Tables {#load-abundance}

This chunk imports PICRUSt2's two native output tables -- the per-sample KO abundance table (aggregated to KEGG pathway level below) and the per-sample MetaCyc pathway abundance table -- stripping the `ko:` prefix PICRUSt2 adds to KO identifiers so it matches what `ko2kegg_abundance()` expects.

```{r load-abundance-tables}
# Read PICRUSt2's native tab-separated output. The first column is the
# feature identifier ("function" for KO, "pathway" for MetaCyc); every
# remaining column is one sample's abundance.
ko_abundance_raw <- read_tsv(input_ko_path, show_col_types = FALSE)

# PICRUSt2's default KO reference database prefixes each KO identifier with
# "ko:" (e.g. "ko:K00001"); strip it so ko2kegg_abundance()'s internal
# KO-to-pathway mapping (which expects the bare "K00001" form) matches.
ko_abundance_raw[[1]] <- gsub("^ko:", "", ko_abundance_raw[[1]])

pathway_abundance_raw <- read_tsv(input_pathway_path, show_col_types = FALSE)

cat(
  "Abundance Tables Loaded:\n",
  "- KO table (input to KEGG pathway conversion):", nrow(ko_abundance_raw), "KOs x",
  ncol(ko_abundance_raw) - 1, "samples\n",
  "- MetaCyc pathway table:", nrow(pathway_abundance_raw), "pathways x",
  ncol(pathway_abundance_raw) - 1, "samples\n"
)
```

## Validate Sample ID Consistency {#validate-samples}

This chunk confirms that the sample identifiers in both abundance tables exactly match [data/metadata.tsv](../../data/metadata.tsv)'s `SampleID` column, so a mismatch is caught here with a clear message rather than surfacing later as a cryptic error inside `pathway_daa()`.

```{r validate-sample-ids}
# Sample columns are every column except the first (feature ID) column, in
# both abundance tables — validate both against metadata so a mismatch in
# either one is caught here rather than surfacing as a cryptic downstream
# error inside pathway_daa().
abundance_sample_ids <- colnames(ko_abundance_raw)[-1]
pathway_sample_ids   <- colnames(pathway_abundance_raw)[-1]
metadata_sample_ids  <- sample_metadata$SampleID

report_sample_mismatch <- function(observed, expected, source_label) {
  missing_from_metadata <- setdiff(observed, expected)
  missing_from_source    <- setdiff(expected, observed)
  if (length(missing_from_metadata) == 0 && length(missing_from_source) == 0) {
    return(invisible(TRUE))
  }
  stop(
    source_label, " sample IDs do not exactly match data/metadata.tsv's SampleID column.\n",
    if (length(missing_from_metadata) > 0)
      paste0("  In ", source_label, " but missing from metadata: ",
             paste(missing_from_metadata, collapse = ", "), "\n") else "",
    if (length(missing_from_source) > 0)
      paste0("  In metadata but missing from ", source_label, ": ",
             paste(missing_from_source, collapse = ", "), "\n") else "",
    "Fix data/metadata.tsv (or confirm you are pointing at the correct Step 2 run) before proceeding."
  )
}
report_sample_mismatch(abundance_sample_ids, metadata_sample_ids, "KO abundance table")
report_sample_mismatch(pathway_sample_ids, metadata_sample_ids, "MetaCyc pathway abundance table")

cat("Sample ID validation passed: all", length(metadata_sample_ids),
    "samples match exactly between metadata and both abundance tables.\n")
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Prepare Both Functional Abundance Matrices {#prepare-functional-abundance}

This chunk builds the two abundance matrices each functional level's DAA methods will actually be run on: the MetaCyc pathway table reshaped with feature IDs as row names, and the KEGG pathway table produced by aggregating the KO table with `ggpicrust2::ko2kegg_abundance()` (see [Why Two Functional Levels?] above). Only the levels listed in `functional_levels_to_analyze` are kept for the analysis that follows.

```{r prepare-functional-abundance}
# MetaCyc: convert the tibble (feature-ID column + sample columns) into a
# data frame with feature IDs as rownames — the format pathway_daa()
# expects for `abundance`.
metacyc_abundance_raw <- pathway_abundance_raw %>%
  column_to_rownames(var = colnames(pathway_abundance_raw)[1]) %>%
  as.data.frame()

# KEGG: aggregate KO predictions with the corrected PICRUSt2-style upper-half
# mean and request ggpicrust2's broad prokaryote filter. This removes
# Organismal Systems and most Human Diseases maps, but cannot guarantee that
# every host/eukaryote/virus-associated map is absent; explicit interpretation
# flags are added during annotation below. The arguments are written explicitly
# so neither aggregation nor broad filtering can change silently if package
# defaults change in a future release.
kegg_abundance_raw <- ko2kegg_abundance(
  data                    = as.data.frame(ko_abundance_raw),
  method                  = "abundance",
  filter_for_prokaryotes  = TRUE,
  progress                = FALSE
)

functional_abundance_by_level <- list(
  MetaCyc = metacyc_abundance_raw,
  KEGG    = kegg_abundance_raw
)
functional_abundance_by_level <- functional_abundance_by_level[functional_levels_to_analyze]

for (level_name in names(functional_abundance_by_level)) {
  cat(
    level_name, "abundance matrix prepared:",
    nrow(functional_abundance_by_level[[level_name]]), "features x",
    ncol(functional_abundance_by_level[[level_name]]), "samples\n"
  )
}
```
