# Analysis Functions {#analysis-functions}

The functions below implement this notebook's per-functional-level pipeline (prevalence filtering, degenerate-sample removal, two-method DAA, annotation, and agreement reporting) once, so the MetaCyc and KEGG runs call identical logic.

## Run the Selected DAA Methods {#fn-run-daa}

The chunk below defines `run_daa_across_methods()`, this notebook's core orchestration function: for each non-reference `Condition` it restricts the data to a clean two-condition subset, runs every requested DAA method against that subset, and standardizes each method's result to a common column set before returning it. The backend fields are named `group1` and `group2`; the code comments explain why those API fields are relabeled from the comparison explicitly rather than trusted as returned.

```{r define-run-daa-across-methods}
# run_daa_across_methods()
#
# Runs one DAA call per requested method, once per non-reference Condition --
# i.e. every comparison this notebook ever performs is the reference Condition
# (from data/metadata.tsv's Reference column) against exactly one
# other Condition, on a sample subset restricted to just those two Conditions. The
# reference Condition is therefore the ONLY Condition every other Condition is ever
# compared against; there is never a condition comparison that skips
# it, and no single DAA call ever sees more than two Condition levels at once.
# Both selected methods go through ggpicrust2::pathway_daa(). This
# two-conditions-at-a-time restriction gives both methods the same comparison
# structure. Restricting every call's
# `metadata`/`abundance` to only the two Conditions under comparison -- and
# dropping unused factor levels from the subset -- guarantees every
# backend always sees a clean two-level factor, regardless of how many
# Condition levels exist in the full dataset.
#
# IMPORTANT -- group1/group2 are always overwritten with the known
# `reference`/`comparison_group` values from this loop, never trusted from
# a backend's own returned data frame. ggpicrust2::pathway_daa() correctly
# relevels the Condition factor for the STATISTICAL model in every backend (so
# p-values are unaffected), but several backends' own result-table
# construction labels the output group1/group2 columns from a stale,
# pre-relevel, alphabetically-sorted factor-levels vector instead of the
# actual releveled factor or the `reference` argument itself. Left
# uncorrected, this
# silently mislabels which Condition is "reference" and which is "comparison"
# for every other method, which is what caused the reference condition to
# appear as the wrong Condition in exported sheets, the log2FoldChange join below to
# produce all-NA log2FoldChange for every affected method, and (because it also
# broke Feature_ID x Condition uniqueness) the Method_Agreement
# pivot_wider() step in Export to error with "Can't convert `fill`
# <character> to <list>". Since this notebook already knows both Conditions
# involved in every call (it constructed the two-condition subset itself),
# there is no need to trust the backend's own labeling at all.
#
# Each tryCatch()-wrapped (method, comparison Condition) call failing does not
# abort any other method or comparison.
#
# Every backend's raw result is also restricted to a fixed canonical column
# set (feature, group1, group2, method, DAA_Submethod, p_values, p_adjust,
# adj_method) before being stored. pathway_daa() otherwise passes through
# whatever extra, backend-native columns the underlying package's own result
# object happens to carry unchanged. Left unrestricted, bind_rows() below unions these
# per-backend columns across every method's rows: a column that only exists
# natively for one backend ends up populated for that backend's rows and NA
# for every other method's rows once combined -- indistinguishable, in the
# exported workbook, from a genuinely broken column. This notebook already
# computes its own method-independent log2FoldChange from condition mean
# abundances (see process_functional_level() below), so no backend-native
# fold-change-like column is ever needed downstream; restricting to the
# canonical set here drops them before they can leak into any exported sheet.
#
# Returns a list with:
#   $results  — a single row-bound data frame of every successful (method,
#               comparison Condition) call's result, restricted to the canonical
#               columns above (group1 is always the reference Condition, group2
#               is always that call's comparison Condition -- see the IMPORTANT
#               note above), with two further changes: a new DAA_Submethod
#               column preserves the original backend label, and 'method'
#               itself is overwritten with the clean requested method name.
#   $failures — a data frame (DAA_Method, Condition, Error_Message) recording
#               which (method, comparison Condition) pair(s) failed and the R
#               error message for reporting in the rendered notebook.
run_daa_across_methods <- function(abundance, metadata, group, methods,
                                    p_adjust_method, reference,
                                    min_nonzero_samples,
                                    strict_pairwise_prevalence_filter) {
  non_reference_groups <- setdiff(sort(unique(metadata[[group]])), reference)
  if (length(non_reference_groups) == 0) {
    stop("No non-reference ", group, " levels remain to compare against the reference (\"", reference, "\").")
  }

  results_list  <- list()
  failures_list <- list()

  for (comparison_group in non_reference_groups) {

    # Restrict to exactly this pair of Conditions' samples, and drop any unused
    # factor levels by coercing back to character -- this is what
    # guarantees every DAA backend below sees a clean, dichotomous grouping
    # variable no matter how many Condition levels the full dataset has.
    pair_metadata <- metadata[metadata[[group]] %in% c(reference, comparison_group), , drop = FALSE]
    pair_metadata[[group]] <- as.character(pair_metadata[[group]])
    rownames(pair_metadata) <- pair_metadata$sample_name
    pair_abundance <- abundance[, colnames(abundance) %in% pair_metadata$sample_name, drop = FALSE]

    # Optional strict pairwise prevalence filter. This happens after the pooled
    # condition-blind filter and is recomputed separately for this exact pair,
    # so an unrelated third condition cannot remove a feature from the current
    # comparison. The same filtered matrix is passed to both methods.
    if (strict_pairwise_prevalence_filter) {
      reference_samples <- pair_metadata$sample_name[
        pair_metadata[[group]] == reference
      ]
      comparison_samples <- pair_metadata$sample_name[
        pair_metadata[[group]] == comparison_group
      ]
      reference_nonzero <- rowSums(
        pair_abundance[, reference_samples, drop = FALSE] != 0
      )
      comparison_nonzero <- rowSums(
        pair_abundance[, comparison_samples, drop = FALSE] != 0
      )
      pairwise_keep <-
        reference_nonzero >= min_nonzero_samples &
        comparison_nonzero >= min_nonzero_samples
      cat(
        "    Strict pairwise prevalence filter for ", reference, " vs. ",
        comparison_group, ": ", nrow(pair_abundance), " -> ",
        sum(pairwise_keep), " features retained.\n", sep = ""
      )
      pair_abundance <- pair_abundance[pairwise_keep, , drop = FALSE]
    }

    for (daa_method_name in methods) {
      cat("    Running DAA method:", daa_method_name, "vs.", comparison_group, "... ")

      daa_attempt <- tryCatch(
        {
          raw_result <- pathway_daa(
            abundance  = pair_abundance,
            metadata   = pair_metadata,
            group      = group,
            daa_method = daa_method_name,
            select     = NULL,
            p.adjust   = p_adjust_method,
            reference  = reference
          )
          list(success = TRUE, data = raw_result, error = NULL)
        },
        error = function(e) list(success = FALSE, data = NULL, error = conditionMessage(e))
      )

      result_key <- paste(daa_method_name, comparison_group, sep = " vs. ")
      if (daa_attempt$success) {
        cat("OK (", nrow(daa_attempt$data), "rows)\n")

        cleaned <- daa_attempt$data
        cleaned$DAA_Submethod <- cleaned$method
        cleaned$method <- daa_method_name

        # Always overwrite group1/group2 with the known reference/
        # comparison_group values from this loop -- see the IMPORTANT note
        # above the function docstring for why the backend's own output
        # labels cannot be trusted here.
        cleaned$group1 <- reference
        cleaned$group2 <- comparison_group

        # Restrict to the canonical column set (see the function docstring
        # above) so backend-native extra columns cannot leak into bind_rows().
        # Any missing canonical column is added as NA so both methods
        # contribute the identical column set.
        canonical_daa_columns <- c(
          "feature", "group1", "group2", "method", "DAA_Submethod",
          "p_values", "p_adjust", "adj_method"
        )
        missing_canonical_columns <- setdiff(canonical_daa_columns, colnames(cleaned))
        for (missing_column in missing_canonical_columns) {
          cleaned[[missing_column]] <- NA
        }
        cleaned <- cleaned[, canonical_daa_columns, drop = FALSE]

        results_list[[result_key]] <- cleaned
      } else {
        cat("FAILED:", daa_attempt$error, "\n")
        failures_list[[result_key]] <- data.frame(
          DAA_Method    = daa_method_name,
          Condition         = comparison_group,
          Error_Message = daa_attempt$error,
          stringsAsFactors = FALSE
        )
      }
    }
  }

  list(
    results  = if (length(results_list) > 0) bind_rows(results_list) else NULL,
    failures = if (length(failures_list) > 0) bind_rows(failures_list) else
      data.frame(DAA_Method = character(0), Condition = character(0), Error_Message = character(0), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  )
}
```

## Annotate Every Tested Feature Once {#fn-annotate}

The first chunk builds a one-row-per-pathway lookup from the KEGG hierarchy bundled with `ggpicrust2`. The second dispatches KEGG and MetaCyc features to their respective bundled references. No network access is required.

```{r define-annotate-kegg-pathways}
# annotate_kegg_pathways()
#
# Uses the corrected long-format ko_to_kegg_reference bundled with
# ggpicrust2 >= 2.5.16. The hierarchy prefixes (e.g. "09100 ") are removed
# from the exported class labels while the stable koXXXXX pathway ID is
# retained as `feature` for joins to the DAA output.
annotate_kegg_pathways <- function(pathway_ids,
                                   host_associated_pathway_ids) {
  # Load the package data into the current function environment. The lookup is
  # local and versioned with ggpicrust2, so routine annotation is reproducible
  # and does not depend on a live KEGG request.
  data("ko_to_kegg_reference", package = "ggpicrust2", envir = environment())
  reference <- as.data.frame(ko_to_kegg_reference)

  # Validate the reference schema explicitly because upstream package-data
  # changes would otherwise create partially annotated output without a clear
  # explanation of which required field disappeared.
  required_reference_columns <- c(
    "pathway_id", "pathway_number", "pathway_name", "level1", "level2"
  )
  missing_reference_columns <- setdiff(required_reference_columns, colnames(reference))
  if (length(missing_reference_columns) > 0) {
    stop(
      "ggpicrust2's bundled ko_to_kegg_reference is missing required column(s): ",
      paste(missing_reference_columns, collapse = ", "),
      ". Re-run setup/install_R_dependencies.R to install a current release."
    )
  }

  # Reduce the long pathway-to-KO reference to one descriptive row per pathway.
  # Numeric hierarchy prefixes are removed from labels while the stable KEGG
  # pathway and map identifiers remain available for joins and auditing.
  annotation_lookup <- reference %>%
    select(all_of(required_reference_columns)) %>%
    distinct() %>%
    transmute(
      feature             = pathway_id,
      pathway_name        = pathway_name,
      pathway_class       = sub("^\\d+\\s+", "", level1),
      pathway_subclass    = sub("^\\d+\\s+", "", level2),
      pathway_map         = paste0("map", pathway_number)
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      # Broad host/eukaryote/virus-associated categories can share genuine
      # microbial KOs. Flag them for interpretation rather than deleting the
      # underlying prediction and hiding why it appeared.
      requires_organism_appropriateness_review =
        feature %in% host_associated_pathway_ids |
        pathway_class == "Organismal Systems" |
        pathway_subclass == "Information processing in viruses",
      organism_appropriateness_note = ifelse(
        requires_organism_appropriateness_review,
        paste0(
          "Review before biological interpretation: this KEGG map is host-, ",
          "eukaryote-, or virus-associated. Shared KOs may still be genuine ",
          "microbial genes, but the map name is not direct evidence that the ",
          "named host/viral process occurs in the microbial community."
        ),
        paste0(
          "No specific host/eukaryote/virus warning was configured for this ",
          "map; it still represents predicted functional potential and should ",
          "be interpreted with its KEGG hierarchy."
        )
      )
    ) %>%
    distinct(feature, .keep_all = TRUE)

  # Start from the requested IDs so unmatched pathways remain visible as rows
  # with missing annotations instead of being silently dropped by an inner join.
  annotated <- tibble(feature = unique(pathway_ids)) %>%
    left_join(annotation_lookup, by = "feature")

  n_missing <- sum(is.na(annotated$pathway_name))
  n_flagged <- sum(
    annotated$requires_organism_appropriateness_review,
    na.rm = TRUE
  )
  cat(
    "    KEGG pathway annotation: ", nrow(annotated),
    " pathway(s) matched against the bundled reference; ", n_missing,
    " missing a name; ", n_flagged,
    " flagged for organism-appropriateness review.\n", sep = ""
  )
  annotated
}
```

This chunk defines a single annotation dispatcher so the main analysis can request standardized feature annotations without duplicating KEGG- and MetaCyc-specific logic.

```{r define-build-annotation-lookup}
# build_annotation_lookup()
#
# Returns one row per unique feature_id with annotation columns, dispatching
# by functional level:
#   - KEGG: annotate_kegg_pathways() above (bundled local KEGG hierarchy).
#   - MetaCyc: ggpicrust2::pathway_annotation()'s bundled local MetaCyc
#     reference table. Since pathway_annotation() looks up
#     daa_results_df$feature internally, this still needs one representative
#     row per feature from daa_results_combined (the row with the smallest
#     adjusted p-value across methods) as its input, purely to satisfy that
#     function's expected input shape.
build_annotation_lookup <- function(feature_ids, functional_level,
                                    daa_results_combined,
                                    host_associated_pathway_ids) {
  if (functional_level == "KEGG") {
    return(annotate_kegg_pathways(
      feature_ids,
      host_associated_pathway_ids = host_associated_pathway_ids
    ))
  }

  # `pathway_annotation()` expects DAA-shaped input even though only the feature
  # identifier is needed for lookup. Select one deterministic row per feature,
  # preferring the smallest available adjusted p-value across methods.
  representative_rows <- daa_results_combined %>%
    mutate(.p_adjust_numeric = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(p_adjust))) %>%
    group_by(feature) %>%
    arrange(is.na(.p_adjust_numeric), .p_adjust_numeric, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    slice(1) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    select(-.p_adjust_numeric) %>%
    as.data.frame()

  annotated <- pathway_annotation(pathway = "MetaCyc", daa_results_df = representative_rows, ko_to_kegg = FALSE)
  # Return only the stable feature key plus newly added annotation fields; DAA
  # columns are joined from the canonical result table elsewhere.
  new_annotation_columns <- setdiff(colnames(annotated), colnames(representative_rows))
  annotated[, c("feature", new_annotation_columns), drop = FALSE]
}
```

## Process One Functional Level End-to-End {#fn-process-level}

The chunk below defines `process_functional_level()`, which chains together every step above into this notebook's full per-level pipeline -- prevalence filtering, degenerate-sample removal, two-method DAA, annotation, condition-wise summary statistics, log2 fold-change, and a per-feature-per-comparison agreement summary -- and returns a single list holding every table the Export section further down needs.

```{r define-process-functional-level}
# process_functional_level()
#
# Runs this notebook's full per-level pipeline: prevalence filtering,
# degenerate-sample removal, two-method DAA (via run_daa_across_methods()),
# annotation (via build_annotation_lookup()), condition-wise summary
# statistics, log2 fold-change, and a per-feature-per-comparison agreement
# summary. Returns a named list holding
# every intermediate and final table the Export section below needs, so
# that section never recomputes anything.
process_functional_level <- function(level_name, abundance_raw, full_metadata,
                                      group_column, reference_group, daa_methods,
                                      p_adjust_method, significance_threshold,
                                      min_nonzero_samples,
                                      strict_pairwise_prevalence_filter,
                                      host_associated_pathway_ids) {

  cat("\nProcessing functional level:", level_name, "\n")

  # ---- Prevalence filtering ---------------------------------------------
  feature_nonzero_sample_counts <- rowSums(abundance_raw != 0)
  low_prevalence_features <- rownames(abundance_raw)[feature_nonzero_sample_counts < min_nonzero_samples]
  filtered_abundance <- abundance_raw[feature_nonzero_sample_counts >= min_nonzero_samples, , drop = FALSE]

  cat(
    "Prevalence filtering:", nrow(abundance_raw), "->", nrow(filtered_abundance),
    "features retained (removed", length(low_prevalence_features), "present in <",
    min_nonzero_samples, "samples).\n"
  )

  # ---- Diagnose and remove degenerate (non-finite / zero-variance)
  #      samples. pathway_daa()'s LinDA backend does not tolerate
  #      zero-variance samples — left uncaught this crashes deep inside MicrobiomeStat::linda()
  #      with an opaque "NA features are filtered!" /
  #      "missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed" error. Removing such
  #      samples once, here, before any DAA method sees this level's
  #      abundance matrix, keeps every method (not just LinDA) on a
  #      well-defined input. ------------------------------------------------
  non_finite_mask <- !is.finite(as.matrix(filtered_abundance))
  if (any(non_finite_mask)) {
    stop(
      level_name, " abundance matrix contains ", sum(non_finite_mask),
      " non-finite value(s) (NA/NaN/Inf) after prevalence filtering. ",
      "Affected feature(s): ", paste(rownames(filtered_abundance)[apply(non_finite_mask, 1, any)], collapse = ", "), ". ",
      "Affected sample(s): ", paste(colnames(filtered_abundance)[apply(non_finite_mask, 2, any)], collapse = ", "), ". ",
      "Inspect the source PICRUSt2 output file(s) for these identifiers before proceeding."
    )
  }

  sample_variances <- apply(filtered_abundance, 2, var)
  zero_variance_samples <- names(sample_variances)[sample_variances == 0 | is.na(sample_variances)]

  if (length(zero_variance_samples) > 0) {
    cat(
      "Removing", length(zero_variance_samples), "sample(s) with zero variance across all",
      nrow(filtered_abundance), level_name, "features (would otherwise crash pathway_daa()'s LinDA backend):\n",
      paste(" -", zero_variance_samples, collapse = "\n"), "\n"
    )
    filtered_abundance <- filtered_abundance[, !(colnames(filtered_abundance) %in% zero_variance_samples), drop = FALSE]
  } else {
    cat("No zero-variance samples detected among the", ncol(filtered_abundance), level_name, "samples.\n")
  }

  level_metadata <- full_metadata[full_metadata$SampleID %in% colnames(filtered_abundance), , drop = FALSE]
  level_metadata <- level_metadata[match(colnames(filtered_abundance), level_metadata$SampleID), , drop = FALSE]

  # ---- Differential abundance analysis, across every requested method ---
  cat("  Running", length(daa_methods), "DAA method(s):\n")
  daa_run <- run_daa_across_methods(
    abundance       = filtered_abundance,
    metadata        = as.data.frame(level_metadata),
    group           = group_column,
    methods         = daa_methods,
    p_adjust_method = p_adjust_method,
    reference       = reference_group,
    min_nonzero_samples = min_nonzero_samples,
    strict_pairwise_prevalence_filter = strict_pairwise_prevalence_filter
  )

  if (is.null(daa_run$results)) {
    stop(
      "Every requested (DAA method, comparison Condition) combination failed for the ", level_name, " level. Errors:\n",
      paste0("  - ", daa_run$failures$DAA_Method, " vs. ", daa_run$failures$Condition, ": ",
             daa_run$failures$Error_Message, collapse = "\n")
    )
  }
  if (nrow(daa_run$failures) > 0) {
    cat(
      "  NOTE:", nrow(daa_run$failures),
      "(DAA method, comparison Condition) combination(s) failed for the", level_name,
      "level; the method error text is printed above:",
      paste0(daa_run$failures$DAA_Method, " vs. ", daa_run$failures$Condition, collapse = ", "), "\n"
    )
  }

  # ---- Annotate every tested feature once (the full retained feature set
  #      from filtered_abundance, not just features a DAA method happened
  #      to return a row for) via build_annotation_lookup() above. --------
  annotation_lookup <- build_annotation_lookup(
    feature_ids          = rownames(filtered_abundance),
    functional_level     = level_name,
    daa_results_combined = daa_run$results,
    host_associated_pathway_ids = host_associated_pathway_ids
  )

  # pathway_daa()'s own convention (consistent across every backend) is
  # group1 = the reference/baseline level (as resolved from `reference`),
  # group2 = the non-reference/comparison level -- i.e. the OPPOSITE of
  # what the names "group1"/"group2" might suggest. Mapping Condition <-
  # group1 here (as an earlier version of this notebook did) makes every
  # row's "Condition" column hold the constant reference_group value, which
  # then fails to match any key in log2fc_long (built only from
  # non-reference conditions) during the full_join below -- silently producing
  # all-NA log2FoldChange for every row. Condition <- group2 / Reference <- group1 is
  # the correct mapping.
  daa_results_annotated <- daa_run$results %>%
    rename(Feature_ID = feature, Condition = group2, Reference = group1, DAA_Method = method) %>%
    mutate(
      p_values = as.numeric(p_values),
      p_adjust = as.numeric(p_adjust)
    ) %>%
    left_join(annotation_lookup %>% rename(Feature_ID = feature), by = "Feature_ID")

  # ---- Condition-wise summary statistics -------------------------------------
  group_levels <- sort(unique(level_metadata[[group_column]]))
  samples_by_group <- lapply(
    setNames(group_levels, group_levels),
    function(g) level_metadata$SampleID[level_metadata[[group_column]] == g]
  )
  non_reference_groups <- setdiff(group_levels, reference_group)

  # Condition-specific prevalence diagnostics are reported regardless of
  # whether the optional strict pairwise filter is enabled. Counts use the
  # exact filtered feature matrix and metadata-defined sample membership.
  group_nonzero_sample_counts <- as.data.frame(
    sapply(
      samples_by_group,
      function(sample_ids) rowSums(
        filtered_abundance[, sample_ids, drop = FALSE] != 0
      )
    ),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
  rownames(group_nonzero_sample_counts) <- rownames(filtered_abundance)
  group_sample_sizes <- vapply(samples_by_group, length, integer(1))
  group_prevalence_percent <- as.data.frame(
    sweep(
      as.matrix(group_nonzero_sample_counts),
      MARGIN = 2,
      STATS = group_sample_sizes,
      FUN = "/"
    ) * 100,
    check.names = FALSE
  )
  rownames(group_prevalence_percent) <- rownames(filtered_abundance)

  pairwise_prevalence_diagnostics <- bind_rows(lapply(
    non_reference_groups,
    function(comparison_group) {
      reference_nonzero <- group_nonzero_sample_counts[[reference_group]]
      comparison_nonzero <- group_nonzero_sample_counts[[comparison_group]]
      tibble(
        Feature_ID = rownames(filtered_abundance),
        Condition = comparison_group,
        Reference = reference_group,
        Reference_Nonzero_Samples = reference_nonzero,
        Reference_Prevalence_Percent =
          group_prevalence_percent[[reference_group]],
        Comparison_Nonzero_Samples = comparison_nonzero,
        Comparison_Prevalence_Percent =
          group_prevalence_percent[[comparison_group]],
        Structural_Zero = reference_nonzero == 0 | comparison_nonzero == 0,
        Below_Pairwise_Prevalence_Threshold =
          reference_nonzero < min_nonzero_samples |
          comparison_nonzero < min_nonzero_samples
      )
    }
  ))
  for (comparison_group in non_reference_groups) {
    comparison_diagnostics <- pairwise_prevalence_diagnostics %>%
      filter(Condition == comparison_group)
    cat(
      "  Pairwise prevalence diagnostics for ", reference_group, " vs. ",
      comparison_group, ": ",
      sum(comparison_diagnostics$Structural_Zero),
      " structural-zero feature(s); ",
      sum(comparison_diagnostics$Below_Pairwise_Prevalence_Threshold),
      " below the per-condition threshold of ", min_nonzero_samples, ".\n",
      sep = ""
    )
  }

  group_mean_abundance <- as.data.frame(
    # Arithmetic condition means are descriptive summaries of predicted
    # abundance; they are not the model coefficients returned by either DAA
    # backend.
    sapply(samples_by_group, function(sample_ids) rowMeans(filtered_abundance[, sample_ids, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
  group_sd_abundance <- as.data.frame(
    # Use sample SD (`stats::sd`, denominator n - 1) within each condition.
    sapply(samples_by_group, function(sample_ids) apply(filtered_abundance[, sample_ids, drop = FALSE], 1, sd, na.rm = TRUE)),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
  group_relative_abundance <- as.data.frame(
    # Normalize the vector of condition means across retained pathways. These
    # proportions are for descriptive reporting and are not fed back into LinDA.
    lapply(group_mean_abundance, function(x) x / sum(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
  rownames(group_relative_abundance) <- rownames(group_mean_abundance)

  # ---- Log2 fold-change vs. reference condition --------------------------
  # Use half the smallest positive condition mean as a level-specific
  # pseudocount. This preserves the direction of features absent from one
  # condition while avoiding infinite fold changes; replacing infinity with
  # zero would incorrectly report "no change" for those boundary features.
  positive_group_means <- unlist(group_mean_abundance, use.names = FALSE)
  positive_group_means <- positive_group_means[is.finite(positive_group_means) & positive_group_means > 0]
  if (length(positive_group_means) == 0) {
    stop("No positive condition mean abundances remain for ", level_name, "; cannot calculate log2 fold-change.")
  }
  log2fc_pseudocount <- min(positive_group_means) / 2
  cat("  Log2 fold-change pseudocount:", format(log2fc_pseudocount, scientific = TRUE), "\n")

  log2fc_columns <- lapply(non_reference_groups, function(g) {
    log2(
      (group_mean_abundance[[g]] + log2fc_pseudocount) /
        (group_mean_abundance[[reference_group]] + log2fc_pseudocount)
    )
  })
  names(log2fc_columns) <- non_reference_groups
  log2fc_wide <- as.data.frame(log2fc_columns, check.names = FALSE)
  rownames(log2fc_wide) <- rownames(group_mean_abundance)
  log2fc_long <- log2fc_wide %>%
    rownames_to_column("Feature_ID") %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = -Feature_ID, names_to = "Condition", values_to = "log2FoldChange")

  # ---- Combine DAA (all methods) + log2FoldChange ------------------------
  daa_all_methods <- daa_results_annotated %>%
    full_join(log2fc_long, by = c("Feature_ID", "Condition")) %>%
    mutate(
      significance = case_when(
        is.na(p_adjust)   ~ NA_character_,
        p_adjust < 0.0001 ~ "****",
        p_adjust < 0.001  ~ "***",
        p_adjust < 0.01   ~ "**",
        p_adjust < 0.05   ~ "*",
        TRUE              ~ ""
      )
    ) %>%
    # Column order: log2FoldChange and significance -- the two figures most
    # people look at first (effect size and whether it is significant) --
    # are placed directly after DAA_Submethod, ahead of the raw p-values,
    # adj_method, and pathway annotation columns that follow via
    # everything(). Applied uniformly to every functional level (not just
    # KEGG) since the underlying column set and this ordering logic are
    # level-agnostic.
    select(
      Feature_ID, Condition, Reference, DAA_Method, DAA_Submethod,
      log2FoldChange, significance,
      everything()
    )

  # ---- Per-feature-per-comparison agreement across the selected methods --
  annotation_columns <- setdiff(
    colnames(daa_all_methods),
    c("Feature_ID", "Condition", "Reference", "DAA_Method", "DAA_Submethod",
      "p_values", "p_adjust", "adj_method", "log2FoldChange", "significance")
  )
  agreement_annotation_lookup <- daa_all_methods %>%
    distinct(Feature_ID, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
    select(all_of(c("Feature_ID", annotation_columns)))

  agreement_summary <- daa_all_methods %>%
    # Summarize method completion and threshold crossings without combining
    # p-values. The resulting label is descriptive convergence evidence only.
    filter(!is.na(DAA_Method)) %>%
    group_by(Feature_ID, Condition, Reference) %>%
    summarise(
      Methods_Completed        = n_distinct(DAA_Method[!is.na(p_adjust)]),
      Significant_Method_Count = sum(p_adjust < significance_threshold, na.rm = TRUE),
      Methods_Significant      = paste(sort(unique(DAA_Method[!is.na(p_adjust) & p_adjust < significance_threshold])), collapse = "; "),
      log2FoldChange           = dplyr::first(log2FoldChange),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      Method_Agreement = case_when(
        Methods_Completed < length(daa_methods) ~ "Incomplete: one method failed",
        Significant_Method_Count == length(daa_methods) ~ "Both methods significant",
        Significant_Method_Count == 0 ~ "Neither method significant",
        TRUE ~ paste0(Methods_Significant, " only")
      )
    ) %>%
    left_join(
      pairwise_prevalence_diagnostics,
      by = c("Feature_ID", "Condition", "Reference")
    ) %>%
    left_join(agreement_annotation_lookup, by = "Feature_ID")

  cat(
    "  Method agreement:", nrow(agreement_summary), "feature x condition comparisons; ",
    sum(agreement_summary$Method_Agreement == "Both methods significant"),
    "significant with both methods.\n"
  )

  list(
    # Return every analysis and diagnostic object required for workbook export.
    # Keeping these in one named object prevents the export phase from silently
    # recomputing statistics with different settings.
    level_name               = level_name,
    filtered_abundance       = filtered_abundance,
    level_metadata           = level_metadata,
    daa_run_failures         = daa_run$failures,
    daa_all_methods          = daa_all_methods,
    agreement_summary        = agreement_summary,
    group_mean_abundance     = group_mean_abundance,
    group_sd_abundance       = group_sd_abundance,
    group_relative_abundance = group_relative_abundance,
    group_nonzero_sample_counts = group_nonzero_sample_counts,
    group_prevalence_percent = group_prevalence_percent,
    pairwise_prevalence_diagnostics = pairwise_prevalence_diagnostics,
    log2fc_wide              = log2fc_wide,
    group_levels             = group_levels,
    annotation_lookup        = annotation_lookup
  )
}
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Run the Analysis for Each Functional Level {#run-analysis}

This chunk calls `process_functional_level()` once per entry in `functional_levels_to_analyze` (MetaCyc and/or KEGG), storing each level's full set of results in `level_results` for the Export section that follows.

```{r run-analysis-per-level}
# Preserve functional-level names on the result list so downstream export never
# infers whether a matrix is MetaCyc or KEGG from its position.
level_results <- lapply(
  setNames(functional_levels_to_analyze, functional_levels_to_analyze),
  function(level_name) {
    process_functional_level(
      # Pass every statistical choice explicitly. This makes the per-level calls
      # auditable and prevents hidden defaults inside the orchestration function.
      level_name              = level_name,
      abundance_raw           = functional_abundance_by_level[[level_name]],
      full_metadata           = sample_metadata,
      group_column            = group_column,
      reference_group         = reference_group,
      daa_methods             = daa_methods_to_run,
      p_adjust_method         = p_adjust_method,
      significance_threshold  = significance_threshold,
      min_nonzero_samples     = min_nonzero_samples,
      strict_pairwise_prevalence_filter = strict_pairwise_prevalence_filter,
      host_associated_pathway_ids = kegg_host_associated_pathway_ids
    )
  }
)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Document and Export Results {#export-results}

This chunk writes each functional level's results to its own Excel workbook: one combined condition-wise `Abundance_Summary` sheet, one sheet per selected DAA method, and a `Method_Agreement` sheet that reports both methods side by side.

```{r export-to-excel}
# One self-contained workbook per functional level (every results table
# for THAT level only) rather than one combined
# workbook with level-prefixed sheet names, so MetaCyc and KEGG results can
# be opened, filtered, and shared independently. Sheet names below are
# therefore unprefixed within each level's own file. Sample metadata itself
# is not re-exported here -- it lives in data/metadata.tsv (see
# data/README.md), which is this workbook's own input, not a result of it.
method_agreement_by_level    <- list()
daa_methods_present_by_level <- list()
abundance_summary_by_level   <- list()
daa_export_by_level          <- list()

for (level_name in names(level_results)) {
  this_level <- level_results[[level_name]]
  this_excel_path <- output_excel_path_by_level[[level_name]]

  # Rebuild each functional-level workbook from scratch on a full run so
  # obsolete sheets from a previous configuration cannot remain.
  if (file.exists(this_excel_path)) {
    unlink(this_excel_path)
  }

  # Sheet: one row per retained pathway, combining all condition-wise mean,
  # SD, relative-abundance, non-zero sample count, prevalence percentage,
  # structural-zero/boundary flags, and comparison-vs-reference log2 fold-
  # change values. Metric names are embedded in the column headers so values
  # from different summaries cannot be confused when filtering or copying.
  non_reference_groups <- setdiff(this_level$group_levels, reference_group)
  abundance_summary <- tibble(Feature_ID = rownames(this_level$group_mean_abundance))
  for (group_name in this_level$group_levels) {
    abundance_summary[[paste0(group_name, "_Mean_Abundance")]] <-
      this_level$group_mean_abundance[[group_name]]
    abundance_summary[[paste0(group_name, "_SD_Abundance")]] <-
      this_level$group_sd_abundance[[group_name]]
    abundance_summary[[paste0(group_name, "_Relative_Abundance")]] <-
      this_level$group_relative_abundance[[group_name]]
    abundance_summary[[paste0(group_name, "_Nonzero_Samples")]] <-
      this_level$group_nonzero_sample_counts[[group_name]]
    abundance_summary[[paste0(group_name, "_Prevalence_Percent")]] <-
      this_level$group_prevalence_percent[[group_name]]
  }
  abundance_summary$Has_Structural_Zero_Condition <- apply(
    this_level$group_nonzero_sample_counts == 0,
    1,
    any
  )
  abundance_summary$Has_Below_Prevalence_Threshold_Condition <- apply(
    this_level$group_nonzero_sample_counts < min_nonzero_samples,
    1,
    any
  )
  for (group_name in non_reference_groups) {
    abundance_summary[[paste0(group_name, "_vs_", reference_group, "_log2FoldChange")]] <-
      this_level$log2fc_wide[[group_name]]
  }
  if (level_name == "KEGG") {
    abundance_summary <- abundance_summary %>%
      left_join(
        this_level$annotation_lookup %>% rename(Feature_ID = feature),
        by = "Feature_ID"
      )
  }
  abundance_summary_by_level[[level_name]] <- abundance_summary
  add_sheet_to_excel(this_excel_path, "Abundance_Summary", abundance_summary,
                     rownames = FALSE, overwrite = TRUE)

  # One sheet PER DAA method (rather than a single combined long table),
  # named after the method itself, dropping the now-redundant DAA_Method
  # column (the sheet name already says which method this is) while keeping
  # the backend's DAA_Submethod label for transparency.
  daa_all_methods_export <- this_level$daa_all_methods
  daa_export_by_level[[level_name]] <- daa_all_methods_export
  daa_methods_present <- sort(unique(daa_all_methods_export$DAA_Method[!is.na(daa_all_methods_export$DAA_Method)]))
  daa_methods_present_by_level[[level_name]] <- daa_methods_present
  for (method_name in daa_methods_present) {
    method_sheet <- daa_all_methods_export %>%
      filter(DAA_Method == method_name) %>%
      select(-DAA_Method) %>%
      arrange(p_adjust)
    add_sheet_to_excel(this_excel_path, method_name, method_sheet,
                       rownames = FALSE, overwrite = TRUE)
  }

  # Sheet: exact adjusted p-values and significance codes for LinDA and
  # MaAsLin2, plus an explicit agreement label. This is a transparent
  # side-by-side comparison, not a majority-vote consensus statistic.
  method_comparison_matrix <- daa_all_methods_export %>%
    filter(!is.na(DAA_Method)) %>%
    select(Feature_ID, Condition, DAA_Method, p_adjust, significance) %>%
    pivot_wider(
      names_from  = DAA_Method,
      values_from = c(p_adjust, significance),
      names_glue  = "{DAA_Method}_{.value}"
    )

  method_agreement <- this_level$agreement_summary %>%
    left_join(method_comparison_matrix, by = c("Feature_ID", "Condition")) %>%
    arrange(
      factor(
        Method_Agreement,
        levels = c("Both methods significant", "LinDA only", "Maaslin2 only",
                   "Neither method significant", "Incomplete: one method failed")
      ),
      Feature_ID
    )
  method_agreement_by_level[[level_name]] <- method_agreement
  add_sheet_to_excel(this_excel_path, "Method_Agreement", method_agreement,
                     rownames = FALSE, overwrite = TRUE)

  cat("Results for", level_name, "exported to:\n ", this_excel_path, "\n")
}
```

## Document and Export Column Dictionary {#column-dictionary}

This chunk documents every column written to every sheet of both workbooks in a trailing `Column_Dictionary` sheet, using the project's shared [build_column_dictionary_function.R](../functions/build_column_dictionary_function.R) helper, which fails loudly if any exported column is missing a description -- so this dictionary cannot silently drift out of sync with what the workbooks actually contain.

```{r build-and-export-column-dictionary}
# Human-readable explanation for every column written to each sheet above.
# build_column_dictionary() fails loudly if any exported column is missing
# from these named vectors, so this dictionary cannot silently drift out of
# sync with what the workbook actually contains.

# build_abundance_summary_column_descriptions()
# Complete description of the combined Abundance_Summary sheet for one
# functional level, including every Condition and comparison-specific column.
build_abundance_summary_column_descriptions <- function(level_name, group_levels,
                                                        reference_group,
                                                        min_nonzero_samples) {
  descriptions <- c(Feature_ID = paste0(level_name, " feature identifier."))

  for (group_name in group_levels) {
    descriptions[paste0(group_name, "_Mean_Abundance")] <-
      paste0("Mean predicted pathway abundance for condition ", group_name, ".")
    descriptions[paste0(group_name, "_SD_Abundance")] <-
      paste0("Sample standard deviation of predicted pathway abundance for condition ", group_name, ".")
    descriptions[paste0(group_name, "_Relative_Abundance")] <- paste0(
      "Condition-mean relative abundance for condition ", group_name,
      ": pathway mean divided by the sum of all retained pathway means in that condition."
    )
    descriptions[paste0(group_name, "_Nonzero_Samples")] <- paste0(
      "Number of samples in condition ", group_name,
      " with predicted pathway abundance greater than zero."
    )
    descriptions[paste0(group_name, "_Prevalence_Percent")] <- paste0(
      "Percentage of samples in condition ", group_name,
      " with predicted pathway abundance greater than zero (0-100 scale)."
    )
  }

  descriptions["Has_Structural_Zero_Condition"] <-
    "TRUE when at least one condition has zero non-zero samples for this feature; the displayed log2 fold-change can then be strongly pseudocount-sensitive."
  descriptions["Has_Below_Prevalence_Threshold_Condition"] <- paste0(
    "TRUE when at least one condition has fewer than min_nonzero_samples (",
    min_nonzero_samples,
    ") non-zero samples. This is a boundary/sparsity flag even when the default pooled prevalence filter retains the feature."
  )

  for (group_name in setdiff(group_levels, reference_group)) {
    descriptions[paste0(group_name, "_vs_", reference_group, "_log2FoldChange")] <- paste0(
      "Pseudocount-stabilized log2(", group_name, " mean abundance / ",
      reference_group, " reference mean abundance); the pseudocount is half the smallest positive condition mean within this functional level."
    )
  }

  if (level_name == "KEGG") {
    descriptions["pathway_name"] <-
      "KEGG pathway name from ggpicrust2's bundled ko_to_kegg_reference hierarchy."
    descriptions["pathway_class"] <-
      "Top-level KEGG hierarchy class from ggpicrust2's bundled reference, with the numeric hierarchy prefix removed."
    descriptions["pathway_subclass"] <-
      "Second-level KEGG hierarchy class from ggpicrust2's bundled reference, with the numeric hierarchy prefix removed."
    descriptions["pathway_map"] <-
      "Generic KEGG map identifier constructed from the bundled pathway number (map#####)."
    descriptions["requires_organism_appropriateness_review"] <-
      "TRUE when this retained KEGG map is configured or hierarchically identified as host-, eukaryote-, or virus-associated and therefore requires explicit organism-appropriateness review before biological reporting."
    descriptions["organism_appropriateness_note"] <-
      "Interpretation note explaining that shared microbial KOs do not prove the named host/eukaryotic/viral pathway process occurs."
  }
  descriptions
}

# build_level_column_descriptions()
# Shared column vocabulary across a level's per-method sheets and the
# Method_Agreement sheet. `method_columns` adds descriptions for the
# method-specific adjusted-p-value and significance-code columns. Any other
# column present but not covered by the fixed vocabulary below is a
# pathway annotation column (KEGG: from the bundled long-format hierarchy;
# MetaCyc: from
# ggpicrust2::pathway_annotation()'s bundled reference table) and is
# described generically as a fallback.
build_level_column_descriptions <- function(level_name, columns_present, reference_group,
                                             p_adjust_method, significance_threshold,
                                             method_columns = character(0)) {
  descriptions <- c(
    Feature_ID               = paste0(level_name, " feature identifier."),
    Condition                     = "Non-reference condition in this pairwise comparison.",
    Reference                 = paste0("Reference/baseline condition this row is compared against (\"", reference_group, "\")."),
    DAA_Submethod              = "Original ggpicrust2 backend label for this method; informational only.",
    p_values                    = "Raw (unadjusted) p-value from this sheet's DAA method.",
    p_adjust                     = paste0("Multiple-testing-adjusted p-value (", p_adjust_method, ") within this method x functional-level x reference-versus-comparison family."),
    adj_method                    = "Multiple-testing correction method used to compute p_adjust for this row (matches p_adjust_method in Configuration).",
    log2FoldChange                 = "Pseudocount-stabilized log2(condition mean abundance / reference-condition mean abundance); the pseudocount is half the smallest positive condition mean within this functional level.",
    significance                   = "Conventional asterisk significance code derived from p_adjust (**** < 0.0001, *** < 0.001, ** < 0.01, * < 0.05).",
    Methods_Completed                = "Number of the two selected DAA methods that returned a result for this Feature_ID x Condition comparison; method failures are reported in the rendered Step 4 notebook.",
    Significant_Method_Count           = paste0("Number of the two selected methods that called this Feature_ID x Condition comparison significant at adjusted p < ", significance_threshold, "."),
    Methods_Significant                  = "Semicolon-separated list of the specific method(s) that called this comparison significant.",
    Method_Agreement                       = "Agreement category: both methods significant, one named method only, neither method significant, or incomplete because one method failed. This is not a combined p-value.",
    Reference_Nonzero_Samples = "Number of reference-condition samples with predicted abundance greater than zero for this feature.",
    Reference_Prevalence_Percent = "Percentage of reference-condition samples with predicted abundance greater than zero (0-100 scale).",
    Comparison_Nonzero_Samples = "Number of comparison-condition samples with predicted abundance greater than zero for this feature.",
    Comparison_Prevalence_Percent = "Percentage of comparison-condition samples with predicted abundance greater than zero (0-100 scale).",
    Structural_Zero = "TRUE when the feature has zero non-zero samples in either the reference or comparison condition; the displayed log2 fold-change can then be strongly pseudocount-sensitive.",
    Below_Pairwise_Prevalence_Threshold = "TRUE when either condition has fewer than min_nonzero_samples non-zero samples. With strict_pairwise_prevalence_filter = TRUE, such a feature is excluded from this pairwise model; with the default FALSE setting, it remains testable but explicitly flagged."
  )
  if (level_name == "KEGG") {
    descriptions["pathway_name"] <- "KEGG pathway name from ggpicrust2's bundled ko_to_kegg_reference hierarchy."
    descriptions["pathway_class"] <- "Top-level KEGG hierarchy class from ggpicrust2's bundled reference, with the numeric hierarchy prefix removed."
    descriptions["pathway_subclass"] <- "Second-level KEGG hierarchy class from ggpicrust2's bundled reference, with the numeric hierarchy prefix removed."
    descriptions["pathway_map"] <- "Generic KEGG map identifier constructed from the bundled pathway number (map#####)."
    descriptions["requires_organism_appropriateness_review"] <- "TRUE when this retained KEGG map is configured or hierarchically identified as host-, eukaryote-, or virus-associated and therefore requires explicit organism-appropriateness review before biological reporting."
    descriptions["organism_appropriateness_note"] <- "Interpretation note explaining that shared microbial KOs do not prove the named host/eukaryotic/viral pathway process occurs."
  }

  if (length(method_columns) > 0) {
    method_column_descriptions <- vapply(method_columns, function(column_name) {
      method_name <- sub("_(p_adjust|significance)$", "", column_name)
      if (grepl("_p_adjust$", column_name)) {
        paste0(method_name, " multiple-testing-adjusted p-value (", p_adjust_method,
               ") for this Feature_ID x Condition comparison.")
      } else {
        paste0(method_name, " significance code derived from its adjusted p-value; blank/NA means not significant or unavailable (method failures are reported in the rendered Step 4 notebook).")
      }
    }, character(1))
    descriptions <- c(descriptions, setNames(method_column_descriptions, method_columns))
  }

  missing_columns <- setdiff(columns_present, names(descriptions))
  if (length(missing_columns) > 0) {
    descriptions <- c(descriptions, setNames(
      rep(if (level_name == "KEGG") "Pathway annotation column (see annotate_kegg_pathways())." else "Pathway annotation column added by ggpicrust2::pathway_annotation().",
          length(missing_columns)),
      missing_columns
    ))
  }
  descriptions[columns_present]
}

# Built and exported once per level's own workbook, using the same
# unprefixed sheet names each workbook actually contains.
for (level_name in names(level_results)) {
  this_level <- level_results[[level_name]]
  this_excel_path <- output_excel_path_by_level[[level_name]]
  abundance_summary        <- abundance_summary_by_level[[level_name]]
  abundance_descriptions   <- build_abundance_summary_column_descriptions(
    level_name, this_level$group_levels, reference_group,
    min_nonzero_samples
  )
  method_agreement        <- method_agreement_by_level[[level_name]]
  daa_methods_present     <- daa_methods_present_by_level[[level_name]]

  # Zero-row slice of daa_all_methods (minus the now-dropped DAA_Method
  # column) as a column-name/type template shared by every per-method
  # sheet -- every method's sheet has the identical schema, so this is
  # computed once rather than once per method.
  method_sheet_template <- daa_export_by_level[[level_name]][
    0,
    setdiff(colnames(daa_export_by_level[[level_name]]), "DAA_Method"),
    drop = FALSE
  ]
  method_dictionary_parts <- lapply(daa_methods_present, function(method_name) {
    build_column_dictionary(method_name, method_sheet_template,
                             build_level_column_descriptions(level_name, colnames(method_sheet_template),
                                                              reference_group, p_adjust_method, significance_threshold),
                             workbook_path = this_excel_path,
                             rownames = FALSE)
  })

  dictionary_parts <- list(
    build_column_dictionary("Abundance_Summary", abundance_summary, abundance_descriptions,
                             workbook_path = this_excel_path, rownames = FALSE),
    bind_rows(method_dictionary_parts),
    build_column_dictionary("Method_Agreement", method_agreement,
                             build_level_column_descriptions(level_name, colnames(method_agreement),
                                                              reference_group, p_adjust_method, significance_threshold,
                                                              method_columns = grep("_(p_adjust|significance)$", colnames(method_agreement), value = TRUE)),
                             workbook_path = this_excel_path, rownames = FALSE)
  )

  column_dictionary <- bind_rows(dictionary_parts)

  add_sheet_to_excel(this_excel_path, "Column_Dictionary", column_dictionary,
                     rownames = FALSE, overwrite = TRUE)

  cat("Column_Dictionary sheet added. ", level_name, " workbook complete at:\n ", this_excel_path, "\n", sep = "")

  print(render_output_links(this_excel_path, labels = paste(level_name, "DAA results workbook (Excel)")))
}
```

# Output Interpretation {#output-interpretation}

[functional_daa_summary_MetaCyc.xlsx](../../results/4_functional_differential_abundance_analysis/functional_daa_summary_MetaCyc.xlsx) and [functional_daa_summary_KEGG.xlsx](../../results/4_functional_differential_abundance_analysis/functional_daa_summary_KEGG.xlsx) are two independent, self-contained workbooks with the same sheet structure (`Abundance_Summary`, `LinDA`, `Maaslin2`, `Method_Agreement`, `Column_Dictionary`) — which workbook you opened tells you the functional level, so sheet names do not repeat it. Sample metadata itself is not included as a sheet; consult `data/metadata.tsv` directly.

-   **`LinDA` and `Maaslin2` sheets**: one row per tested feature x non-reference-condition comparison, containing each method's full results. Interpret adjusted p-values together with the method-independent `log2FoldChange` and remember that the outcome is predicted functional potential. Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment controls FDR within this method x functional-level x comparison family, not across the entire study.
-   **`Abundance_Summary` sheet**: one row per feature retained by the pooled prevalence filter. Every condition has clearly labeled mean-abundance, SD-abundance, relative-abundance, non-zero-sample-count, and prevalence-percentage columns. `Has_Structural_Zero_Condition` and `Has_Below_Prevalence_Threshold_Condition` make sparse boundary cases visible without deleting possible presence/absence contrasts. Every non-reference condition also has a `<comparison>_vs_<reference>_log2FoldChange` column containing `log2((comparison mean + pseudocount)/(reference mean + pseudocount))`; when a structural-zero flag is TRUE, its magnitude is especially pseudocount-sensitive. The KEGG workbook additionally includes pathway hierarchy plus `requires_organism_appropriateness_review` and a plain-language interpretation note.
-   **`Method_Agreement` sheet**: one row per tested feature x comparison with the exact LinDA and MaAsLin2 adjusted p-values, their significance codes, pairwise non-zero/prevalence diagnostics, structural-zero and below-threshold flags, and `Method_Agreement`. “Both methods significant” is the strongest convergence category; “LinDA only” or “Maaslin2 only” is method-dependent. The agreement label is not a combined p-value. If `strict_pairwise_prevalence_filter = TRUE`, below-threshold features are absent because neither method receives them; with the default `FALSE`, they remain visible and flagged.
-   **Small-cohort interpretation**: review the condition sample counts printed in [Load Metadata](#load-metadata). When groups are small relative to the hundreds of pathways tested, treat adjusted-p discoveries as hypothesis-generating and seek independent validation rather than presenting them as definitive.

# Appendix: Troubleshooting Guide

## Common Issues and Solutions

### `Could not find the expected input file`

**Cause**: [Step 2](2_picrust2_pipeline.md) has not been run yet, or its output is still gzip-compressed (`decompress_output_files <- FALSE` was used).

**Action**: Run [Step 2](2_picrust2_pipeline.md) with `decompress_output_files <- TRUE`, or manually decompress `pred_metagenome_unstrat.tsv.gz` / `path_abun_unstrat.tsv.gz`.

### Sample ID mismatch error

**Cause**: [data/metadata.tsv](../../data/metadata.tsv)'s `SampleID` column does not exactly match the sample columns in the PICRUSt2 output (case, whitespace, or a sample present in one but not the other).

**Action**: Compare the mismatched IDs printed in the error message directly against [data/metadata.tsv](../../data/metadata.tsv) and the header row of [pred_metagenome_unstrat.tsv](../../results/2_picrust2_pipeline/picrust2_out_pipeline/KO_metagenome_out/pred_metagenome_unstrat.tsv); fix the metadata file (this is the far more common source of the mismatch than the PICRUSt2 output itself).

### `Reference` column missing, inconsistent, or not exactly one `TRUE` condition

**Cause**: This notebook derives its DAA reference/control group from a `Reference` column in [data/metadata.tsv](../../data/metadata.tsv) (`TRUE` for every row in the reference `Condition`, `FALSE` for every other row) rather than a hardcoded Configuration parameter — see [Load Metadata] and [data/README.md](../../data/README.md). This error group covers three distinct problems, each with its own message: the `Reference` column is missing entirely, a `Condition`'s rows disagree on `Reference` (some `TRUE`, some `FALSE`), or zero / more than one `Condition` is marked `Reference = TRUE`.

**Action**: Add or fix the `Reference` column in [data/metadata.tsv](../../data/metadata.tsv) so that it contains only `TRUE`/`FALSE`, every row of a given `Condition` shares the same value, and exactly one `Condition` is `TRUE` (the intended reference/control condition). See the required schema in [data/README.md](../../data/README.md).

### Some (DAA method, comparison Condition) combinations are missing from a level's results

**Cause**: `run_daa_across_methods()` (see [Run the Selected DAA Methods]) restricts every `pathway_daa()` call to exactly two Conditions: the reference and one comparison Condition at a time (see [Why LinDA and MaAsLin2?]). It deliberately catches and logs, rather than propagates, an individual method/comparison failure. Common causes include:

-   **Sample size or sparsity** — MaAsLin2 can fail if the pairwise subset has too few informative non-zero values for its model.
-   **Degenerate transformed data** — LinDA can fail if zero-variance sample removal was insufficient for a particular comparison.

**Action**: Read the method error printed in the rendered Step 4 notebook for the specific method/Condition/level — it is the underlying package's own error text. A failure for one (method, comparison Condition) combination does not affect any other combination, method, or functional level; the notebook continues and reports results from every combination that succeeded.

### A DAA method's `log2FoldChange` column is empty, or the wrong `Condition` appears as the reference in exported sheets

**Cause**: Some `ggpicrust2::pathway_daa()` backends have historically constructed output `group1`/`group2` labels from factor order rather than the explicit reference. This can break the join to the notebook's method-independent log2 fold-change.

**Action**: Nothing to do — `run_daa_across_methods()` (see [Run the Selected DAA Methods] in Analysis Functions) now always overwrites `group1`/`group2` with the known `reference`/`comparison_group` values from its own loop, for every method, rather than trusting any backend's self-reported labels. If you still see an empty `log2FoldChange` column or an unexpected reference `Condition` after re-running, that specific (method, Condition) combination most likely failed outright; inspect the method error printed in the rendered Step 4 notebook rather than treating it as silent mislabeling.

### A per-method sheet has a stray, mostly-empty column not documented in `Column_Dictionary`

**Cause**: `ggpicrust2::pathway_daa()` can pass through extra backend-native columns in addition to the standard result columns. Combining backends with `bind_rows()` would otherwise create method-specific, mostly-empty columns.

**Action**: `run_daa_across_methods()` (see [Run the Selected DAA Methods] in Analysis Functions) now restricts every method's cleaned result to a fixed canonical column set (`feature`, `group1`, `group2`, `method`, `DAA_Submethod`, `p_values`, `p_adjust`, `adj_method`) immediately after cleaning, before `bind_rows()` combines methods — so no backend-native extra column can reach any exported sheet. This notebook's own `log2FoldChange` (computed from condition mean abundances, method-independent) is added back in afterward and is the only fold-change-like column any sheet ever shows. If you still see a stray column, it is most likely a genuine pathway annotation column (documented generically in `Column_Dictionary` — see [Document and Export Column Dictionary]) rather than a backend leak.

### A KEGG pathway is missing `pathway_name`/`pathway_class` after annotation

**Cause**: The retained pathway ID is absent from the `ko_to_kegg_reference` bundled with the installed `ggpicrust2` release, or that reference has an unexpected schema.

**Action**: Re-run [setup/install_R_dependencies.R](../../setup/install_R_dependencies.R) to install the required current `ggpicrust2` release. Step 4 reports the number of unmatched pathway IDs and does not depend on transient network access.

### `Error in pathway_annotation(): unused argument (...)`

**Cause**: This notebook calls `pathway_annotation()` only for MetaCyc; KEGG annotation uses the bundled reference directly. The installed `ggpicrust2` release may not match the expected MetaCyc API.

**Action**: Run `args(ggpicrust2::pathway_annotation)` in your R console to see your installed version's actual parameter list, and update `ggpicrust2` (`install.packages("ggpicrust2")` or re-run [setup/install_R_dependencies.R](../../setup/install_R_dependencies.R)) to pick up the current CRAN release.

### `pathway_daa()` fails immediately with a package-not-found error for every method

**Cause**: The MaAsLin2 or MicrobiomeStat backend was not installed.

**Action**: Re-run [setup/install_R_dependencies.R](../../setup/install_R_dependencies.R), which installs both selected backends.
